title: Top Pillows for Side, Back & Stomach Sleepers (2026)
summary: The Coop Original Adjustable is the best pillow for most sleepers, with the Saatva Latex for luxury and the Beckham Hotel Collection for budget.
method: Picks come from Tom's Guide (11 pillows, each tested for two weeks; updated Oct 6, 2026) and TechRadar's hands-on pillow guide. Note that TechRadar's page text was last updated in April 2024, so we use it only to corroborate. The Saatva Latex, Layla Kapok, Purple Harmony and Beckham pillows appear in both.
assumptions: Prices change often, so we quote only what the sources show. The two outlets disagree on a few care and cooling details, which we flag. The Coop Original Adjustable is covered by Tom's Guide alone. Pillow choice is personal, so a sleep trial matters.

products.name: Coop Sleep Goods Original Adjustable Pillow
why: Tom's Guide names the Coop Original Adjustable its best pillow overall. You add or remove the foam-and-microfiber fill to set your own height, and it stays medium-firm either way, so it suits side, back and stomach sleepers.
Tom's Guide praises the premium feel at under $100 and the long 100-night trial. Only Tom's Guide covers it in our sources.
specs: Memory foam and microfiber blend, adjustable fill
Medium-firm support for all sleep positions
Tom's Guide lists a queen at $89; check the current price
cons: Needs regular fluffing to keep its shape
Not ideal for chronic hot sleepers
products.best_for: Anyone who wants to tune the height and firmness themselves
products.skip_if: You sleep very hot or hate fluffing your pillow

products.name: Saatva Latex Pillow
why: Tom's Guide says the Saatva Latex Pillow delivers on every promise: responsive support, a naturally cool cotton cover and a hotel feel that needs no re-fluffing. TechRadar also calls it one of the most comfortable and supportive pillows it has tested and worth the investment.
It combines a shredded latex core with a down-alternative outer layer in an organic cotton cover, and comes in two lofts.
specs: Shredded latex core with down-alternative fill, organic cotton cover
Two loft options, roughly 5 or 7 inches (Tom's Guide)
45-night returns, 1-year warranty and free shipping per Tom's Guide
Both outlets show $165; check the current price
pros: Two lofts to fit your sleep position
cons: Outlets disagree on washing: Tom's Guide says not machine washable, TechRadar says the cover and outer fill are
Some find it less soft than a down pillow
products.best_for: Side and back sleepers who want a long-lasting luxury pillow
products.skip_if: You are on a budget or want a classic down feel

products.name: Layla Kapok Pillow
why: Tom's Guide picks the Layla Kapok as best for neck pain, thanks to a firm, adjustable fill of shredded memory foam and kapok fibers that holds its shape better than Coop's. TechRadar also recommends it, calling its high loft especially good for side sleepers.
You can remove fill to change the height, and the cover is machine washable.
specs: Shredded memory foam and kapok fiber, adjustable
About 7 inch loft before removing fill (Tom's Guide)
30-night trial, 5-year warranty, free shipping and returns
Both outlets show $114; check the current price
cons: Tom's Guide says breathable but not cool, while TechRadar credits copper-fiber cooling
Firm feel is not for everyone
products.best_for: Side and back sleepers with neck or shoulder aches
products.skip_if: You want a soft, sink-in pillow or need dedicated cooling

products.name: Purple Harmony Pillow
products.badge: Best for back and combo sleepers
why: Tom's Guide names the Purple Harmony its best for back sleepers: a soft, responsive pillow with a Talalay latex core inside Purple's GelFlex grid that suits back and side sleepers. TechRadar's reviewer called the feel ridiculously squiggly, almost toy-like, yet got some of the best sleep of her life.
The grid keeps it cooler than most foam pillows, though neither outlet sells it as a dedicated cooling pillow.
specs: Talalay latex plus hyper-elastic polymer grid
Multiple loft options (sources say two or three)
Tom's Guide describes list pricing in the premium tier; widgets showed sale prices from about $159; check the current price
pros: Good for back and combo sleepers
cons: The unusual squishy feel won't suit everyone
Tom's Guide says spot clean only, TechRadar says the cover is washable
products.best_for: Back and combination sleepers willing to splurge
products.skip_if: You want a traditional pillow feel or have a small budget

products.name: Beckham Hotel Collection Gel Pillow
why: Tom's Guide says the Beckham Hotel Collection was its top budget pillow until the SquishPillow arrived, and still recommends it as luxury on a budget. TechRadar's tester found it supportive and comfortable for side sleepers and great value.
It is sold as a two-pack, which is part of why the price is so low.
specs: Sold in packs of two; Tom's Guide cites about $59.99 for the pair
pros: Holds its shape for side sleepers
cons: Loft and firmness are not adjustable
Tom's Guide rates it a notch below its top picks
products.best_for: Budget shoppers and side sleepers who want two decent pillows
products.skip_if: You sleep hot or want to adjust the height

tips.title: How to choose
items: Tom's Guide says side sleepers need a high loft to fill the shoulder gap, while back and stomach sleepers do fine with lower loft.
Soft suits stomach sleepers, firm helps side sleepers keep neck and back aligned, and medium-firm works for back and combo sleepers.
Memory foam contours but can run warm, latex is naturally cooler, and allergy sufferers should skip feathers for a down alternative.
TechRadar recommends at least three weeks to judge a pillow; Tom's Guide says to replace pillows every one to two years.

faq: Which pillow is best for stomach sleepers?
Tom's Guide picks the low-loft Helix Talalay Latex Pillow, since stomach sleepers need a thin pillow to prevent neck strain.
What is the best cheap pillow?
Tom's Guide's best cheap pick is the Squishmallows SquishPillow, under $30 in a standard size, though it lacks cooling features.
I sleep hot. What should I buy?
Tom's Guide's best cooling pillow is the Casper Hybrid Pillow with Snow Technology, which scored 5/5 for temperature regulation in its tests.
